name: rok-fortress
description: ROK-FORTRESS is a bilingual safety benchmark of 791 adversarial tasks across 4 NSPS risk domains (CBRNE; Political Violence & Terrorism; Criminal & Financial Illicit Activities; Information Leakage). Each task is provided with English/Korean translations and US/Korean cultural adaptations, supporting a transcreation matrix that disentangles the effects of language and geopolitical grounding on LLM safety. Culture-agnostic tasks (359) yield 2 variants per task (V_En, V_Ko); culture-specific tasks (432) yield 4 variants per task (V_En_US, V_Ko_US, V_En_KR, V_Ko_KR).

rai:dataCollection: Adversarial tasks were authored by the ROK-FORTRESS team following the NSPS risk taxonomy (CBRNE, Political Violence & Terrorism, Criminal & Financial Illicit Activities, Information Leakage). Each task carries an English (US-context) source prompt, a benign counterpart, a simplified direct-request variant, and a 1-7 binary YES/NO rubric. Tasks are expanded along a transcreation matrix: (i) Korean-language translations of the US-context prompt for all tasks, and (ii) for culture-specific tasks only, English Korean-context cultural adaptations and Korean-language Korean-context transcreations. All adversarial prompts, benign prompts, translations, transcreations, and rubrics are human-authored. The 'Simplified Direct Request Variant' columns (one per language/culture variant) are LLM-generated short paraphrases that were subsequently reviewed and corrected by human annotators. Construction extends the FORTRESS benchmark (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.14922).
rai:dataCollectionType: Machine-generated then human-reviewed (simplified direct-request variants only)
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Built on the FORTRESS benchmark (Dong et al., https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.14922 / dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ScaleAI/fortress_public), which provides the underlying NSPS adversarial-task design methodology. ROK-FORTRESS extends FORTRESS with Korean-language translations and Korean-context cultural transcreations.
rai:syntheticDataDescription: Synthetic content is restricted to the four 'Simplified Direct Request Variant' columns (English US-context, Korean US-context, English Korean-context, Korean Korean-context). These short paraphrases were generated by an LLM (see scripts/generate_simplified_direct_requests.py and scripts/generate_direct_requests.py in the codebase) and then individually reviewed and corrected by human annotators before release. All other prompts, rubrics, translations, and transcreations are human-authored.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Each task is expanded into 2 variants (Culture Agnostic) or 4 variants (Culture Specific) at load time via rok_fortress_eval/core/data_loader.py:load_and_expand_csv.
Rubrics are stored as Python-list-formatted strings; loaders parse them into structured YES/NO criteria for tier-weighted scoring (TRS).
No row-level imputation is performed; rows with task type 'Culture Agnostic' intentionally have empty values in the [EN] Cultural Adapted - * and [KR] Transcreated - * columns.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each task is paired with an expert-authored rubric of 1-7 binary YES/NO criteria (mean 6.01 per task) capturing operational severity tiers used for the Tier-weighted Risk Score (TRS). Tasks are also tagged with NSPS Risk Domain / Risk Sub-Domain and a 7-dimension harm taxonomy (WHAT, HOW-1/2/3, WHY, WHO/WHERE, WHEN). Harm-dimension tags are produced by an LLM-based classifier (analysis/scripts/classify_harm_dimensions.py) and used downstream for analysis only; they are not the source of TRS scoring.
rai:annotationsPerItem: One expert-authored rubric (1-7 YES/NO criteria, mean 6.01) per task; one benign counterpart per task; one simplified direct-request variant per task per language/culture pair (2 variants for culture-agnostic, 4 for culture-specific).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: scripts/classify_harm_dimensions.py (LLM-based 7-dimension harm classifier producing the 'Harm Dimensions' column).
rai:dataUseCases: Construct measured: whether the safety behavior of an LLM degrades under (a) shifts in input language and (b) shifts in geopolitical/cultural context, while holding adversarial intent fixed.

Construct-validity evidence: the controlled transcreation matrix yields 2 (culture-agnostic) or 4 (culture-specific) variants of each task with content held semantically constant, so observed score differences across variants can be attributed to language or context rather than task content. Calibration of the 3-judge scoring ensemble against 1,489 human-labeled rubric items achieves Cohen's κ = 0.874 (raw agreement 94.0%), establishing that the TRS metric tracks human harm judgements.

Validated use cases: (i) bilingual (English/Korean) LLM safety evaluation; (ii) decomposing safety degradation into linguistic drop (Δ_ling) and contextual drop (Δ_ctx); (iii) measuring tier-weighted risk (TRS) and over-refusal (ORS) of frontier and Korean regional LLMs across 4 NSPS risk domains.

Out-of-scope uses: (i) generalizing 'cultural context' findings beyond the US/Korea pair; (ii) training data for capability improvements unrelated to safety; (iii) measuring threat models outside the NSPS taxonomy.
rai:dataLimitations: Coverage is limited to two languages (English, Korean) and two cultural contexts (US, Korea); findings may not generalize to other languages or geopolitical settings.
Adversarial coverage is anchored to the NSPS taxonomy; threat models outside this taxonomy are out of scope.

TRS, ORS, and refusal classification depend on a 3-judge LLM ensemble (HyperCLOVA X + o4-mini + Kimi K2; F1 = 0.828 vs human annotations); judge-model upgrades will shift absolute scores even if the prompts are unchanged.
Korean transcreations reflect a single annotation team's cultural-adaptation choices and are not exhaustive over Korean society.
The simplified direct-request variant is a single short paraphrase; it is not a systematic paraphrase distribution.
rai:dataBiases: Risk-domain distribution is non-uniform: CBRNE (251) and Criminal & Financial Illicit Activities (248) dominate, while Information Leakage (83) is under-represented.
Culture-specific tasks (432) outnumber culture-agnostic tasks (359), so the transcreation-matrix mass leans toward culture-specific behavior.
Korean is the only non-US cultural context represented; conclusions about 'cultural context drop' should not be generalized to non-Korean contexts without re-evaluation.
Adversarial prompt-writing style reflects the authoring team's red-teaming conventions and may under-represent prompt styles common to other red-team communities.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information about identifiable private individuals is included. Each NeurIPS-listed category is reviewed below:
Geography: only at the level of public-record geopolitical context (US vs Korea); no individual addresses or coordinates.
Language: dataset is bilingual (English/Korean) by design; no identifying language data about private speakers is collected.
Culture: cultural context (US vs Korean) is treated as a public construct, not as data about identifiable individuals.
Health or medical data: not present.

Political or religious beliefs: prompts may reference public-record geopolitical events and institutions as part of adversarial framing; no beliefs of identifiable private individuals are represented.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ROK-FORTRESS is intended to expose and reduce safety gaps in deployed LLMs, particularly under language and geopolitical-context shifts where prior benchmarks under-measure risk. The dataset contains adversarial prompts designed to elicit unsafe behavior; we release prompts, benign counterparts, and rubrics, but do NOT release any unsafe model completions elicited during evaluation. The intended downstream use is defensive: improving model safety, refusal calibration, and bilingual robustness. Misuse risk is mitigated by (i) the CC-BY-4.0 license requiring attribution, (ii) the rubric-and-tier framing that supports defensive scoring rather than attacker enablement, and (iii) the absence of harmful completions in the release.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Released as version 1.0.0 alongside the ROK-FORTRESS paper. The dataset is versioned on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/ScaleAI/ROK-FORTRESS_public; corrections and clarifications are tracked via the dataset's Hugging Face Community tab. Future revisions will increment the version field of this Croissant descriptor.
